contents.text: Lewis structures represent how valence electrons are arranged in an atom, molecule, or ion. Follow these general guidelines for determining the Lewis structure of a molecule or ion.

elements.text: All the valence electrons of the atoms in a molecule or ion must appear in the Lewis structure. A line between atoms represents two shared electrons. A dot represents an electron that is not shared.

The central atom is the least electronegative element and tends to appear least frequently in the chemical formula. Remember that electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period on the periodic table and decreases as you move down a group. Hydrogen has a full valence shell with only two electrons, so it is never the central atom.
Each atom in the Lewis structure usually has a full valence shell. For most atoms, this means a complete octet, or eight valence electrons.

contents.text: Lewis structures represent how valence electrons are arranged in an atom, molecule, or ion. Follow these general guidelines for determining the Lewis structure of a molecule or ion.

elements.text: All the valence electrons of the atoms in a molecule or ion must appear in the Lewis structure. A line between atoms represents two shared electrons. A dot represents an electron that is not shared.

The central atom is the least electronegative element and tends to appear least frequently in the chemical formula. Remember that electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period on the periodic table and decreases as you move down a group. Hydrogen has a full valence shell with only two electrons, so it is never the central atom.
Each atom in the Lewis structure usually has a full valence shell. For most atoms, this means a complete octet, or eight valence electrons.
